senses.gloss: A particular way of explaining events that supports one side's point of view.
examples: The campaign lost control of the *narrative* after the leak.
Both sides are pushing competing *narratives* about who started the fight.
That *narrative* falls apart as soon as you look at the numbers.

senses.gloss: A national championship competition, usually spoken of in the plural.
examples: Her team qualified for *nationals* for the first time in years.
He finished fourth at *nationals* last spring.
Winners of the regional meet go on to *nationals* in July.

senses.gloss: The fact that something must be done or cannot be avoided.
examples: We sold the car out of *necessity*, not because we wanted to.
There's no *necessity* for you to come along.
*Necessity* forced them to move in with her parents.

senses.gloss: A piece of developed photographic film in which light and dark are reversed.
examples: She found the old *negatives* in a shoebox in the attic.
The lab can print another copy if you still have the *negative*.
Hold the *negative* up to the light and you can just make out his face.

senses.gloss: The linking of computers so that they can share files and connections.
examples: Her degree is in *networking* and systems administration.
He teaches an evening class on *networking* and server security.
The office upgrade covered new *networking* gear and faster wiring.

senses.gloss: The quality of being honorable and generous in character.
examples: There was real *nobility* in the way he accepted the loss.
She admired the quiet *nobility* of her grandmother's life.
The film finds *nobility* in ordinary work.

senses.gloss: A short note written down as a record.
examples: The nurse made a *notation* in his chart.
Her copy of the script was covered in penciled *notations*.
I found a *notation* in the margin explaining the change.

senses.gloss: A small portable computer, more often called a laptop.
examples: He travels with a light *notebook* instead of a full desktop.
The store had a sale on *notebooks* and tablets.
Her *notebook* only gets about four hours on a charge.

senses.gloss: An official act of informing someone, or the notice that does it.
examples: You'll get written *notification* of the decision within ten days.
The school sends *notification* to parents before any field trip.
The bank gave no *notification* that the fee had gone up.

senses.gloss: The practice of doing what a person, law, or rule requires.
examples: The army expects complete *obedience* to orders.
He was raised to value *obedience* above everything else.
*Obedience* to the law is not optional, the judge told him.

senses.gloss: A remark or comment about something you have noticed.
examples: That's a fair *observation*, and I don't have a good answer to it.
She made a few sharp *observations* about the new manager.
He offered the *observation* that nobody had actually read the contract.

senses.gloss: Something a company, studio, or restaurant makes available to the public.
examples: The studio's latest *offering* is a remake of a 1970s thriller.
The menu's vegetarian *offerings* have gotten much better.
Their new *offering* costs half what the competition charges.

senses.gloss: A sale of shares in a company to investors.
examples: The company raised two billion dollars in its public *offering*.
Shares jumped on the first day of the *offering*.
They delayed the stock *offering* until the market settled down.

senses.gloss: A referee, umpire, or other person who enforces the rules at a sporting event.
examples: The *officials* huddled for several minutes before making the call.
An *official* threw a flag on the play.
Fans booed the *officials* as they left the field.

senses.gloss: A planned action carried out by soldiers, police, or rescue workers.
examples: The rescue *operation* went on all through the night.
Federal agents ran a year-long *operation* against the gang.
*Operations* along the border have been scaled back.

senses.gloss: A business or organized activity, or the place where it is run.
examples: They run a small farming *operation* outside of Boise.
The whole *operation* employs about forty people.
Police shut down an illegal gambling *operation* downtown.

senses.gloss: The working of a machine, system, or law, or the fact that it is working.
examples: The manual explains the safe *operation* of the saw.
The new rules come into *operation* in January.
Quiet *operation* is the main selling point of this dishwasher.

senses.gloss: Someone who is against a plan, idea, or law.
examples: *Opponents* of the bill packed the hearing room.
She became the leading *opponent* of the pipeline.
Even *opponents* admit the program has saved money.

senses.gloss: Strong disagreement with a plan or idea, and the effort to stop it.
examples: The proposal met fierce *opposition* from neighbors.
There's growing *opposition* to the new tax.
The bill passed despite *opposition* from both parties.

senses.gloss: The way something is arranged, or the skill of keeping things in order.
examples: The essay has good ideas but poor *organization*.
Her *organization* is what keeps the whole office running.
The *organization* of these files makes no sense to me.

senses.gloss: The direction in which something faces or is placed.
examples: The house's *orientation* keeps the porch shaded all afternoon.
Change the page *orientation* to landscape before you print.
The panels' *orientation* was adjusted to catch more sun.

senses.gloss: The sex a person is romantically attracted to, usually called sexual orientation.
examples: The policy bans discrimination based on sexual *orientation*.
She never hid her *orientation* from her coworkers.
The survey asked about age, race, and sexual *orientation*.
